meaning: Cosy, sociable and pleasant – the warm feeling of good company.
example_af: Die kuier om die vuur was baie gesellig.
example_en: The get-together around the fire was really cosy.
note: Use it for a place, an evening or a person who is good company.

meaning: To visit, socialise or spend relaxed time with friends or family.
example_af: Ons gaan Saterdag by my ouma kuier.
example_en: We're going to visit my grandmother on Saturday.
note: A South African favourite: "kom kuier!" is a warm invitation, and "'n kuier" is a get-together.

meaning: Snacks and food you pack to eat on a road trip.
example_af: Ma het padkos vir die lang rit Kaap toe ingepak.
example_en: Mom packed padkos for the long drive to Cape Town.
note: Literally "road food" (pad = road, kos = food); South Africans use it even when speaking English.

meaning: Nice, tasty or enjoyable – anything that is really good.
note: A true South African favourite: say "lekker!" for anything great, and "slaap lekker" means sleep well.

example_af: My suster verjaar volgende week, so hou ons 'n partytjie.
example_en: My sister has her birthday next week, so we're having a party.
note: Afrikaans uses a verb for this: "Wanneer verjaar jy?" means "When is your birthday?"

meaning: Ouch! – what you say when something hurts.
example_af: Eina! Ek het my toon teen die tafel gestamp.
example_en: Ouch! I stubbed my toe against the table.
note: A proudly South African word, also used in English here; "Dit is eina" means "That's sore".

example_af: Kyk, daar sit 'n pragtige skoenlapper op die blom!
example_en: Look, there's a beautiful butterfly sitting on the flower!
note: Literally "shoe patcher"; the plural is skoenlappers.

example_af: Ek is so moeg ná die lang dag by die werk.
example_en: I'm so tired after the long day at work.
note: Use "moeg vir" to say you're fed up with something, e.g. "Ek is moeg vir die reën" (I'm tired of the rain).

meaning: Slowly, or at a slow pace.
example_af: Ry asseblief stadig, want die pad is nat.
example_en: Please drive slowly, because the road is wet.
note: Also used as an adjective ("'n stadige trein" – a slow train); "stadig maar seker" means slowly but surely.

example_af: Wat is jou planne vir die naweek?
example_en: What are your plans for the weekend?
note: Friends often say "Lekker naweek!" on a Friday – "Have a nice weekend!"

meaning: An insect or bug, any small creepy-crawly.
example_af: Daar is 'n gogga in my koffie!
example_en: There's a bug in my coffee!
note: South Africans use gogga in English too; the plural is goggas and a tiny one is a goggatjie.

example_af: Sy glimlag altyd wanneer sy haar hond sien.
example_en: She always smiles when she sees her dog.
note: The past tense is het geglimlag, and the same word is also a noun: 'n glimlag means a smile.

meaning: Just, simply, for no particular reason.
example_af: Ek het hom sommer gebel om te hoor hoe dit gaan.
example_en: I just called him to hear how he's doing.
note: South Africans use sommer in English too, e.g. 'I did it sommer', meaning just because or without a special reason.

meaning: Curious; eager to know or find out about something.
example_af: Die kinders was baie nuuskierig oor wat in die groot boks is.
example_en: The children were very curious about what was in the big box.
note: It starts with nuus (news), so think 'eager for news'; depending on tone it can also mean nosy.

meaning: A rainbow – the arc of colours you see in the sky when the sun shines after rain.
example_af: Na die donderstorm was daar 'n pragtige reënboog oor die berge.
example_en: After the thunderstorm there was a beautiful rainbow over the mountains.
note: It is reën (rain) + boog (arch, bow); the two dots on the ë show that the e and the second e are pronounced separately: re-ën-boog.

meaning: To forget; to fail to remember something.
example_af: Moenie vergeet om jou sambreel saam te neem nie.
example_en: Don't forget to take your umbrella with you.
note: Verbs starting with ver- don't take ge- in the past tense: ek het vergeet (I forgot).
